content_preview.title: AWS Glue 6.0 Ships With 30% Lower Pricing and Full Apache Iceberg v3 Support
content_preview.summary: AWS Glue 6.0 launches with 30% lower pricing, complete Apache Iceberg v3 support built on Iceberg 1.11.0, and a modernized Spark 4.1 runtime.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Amazon Web Services has announced the general availability of AWS Glue 6.0, a new version of its serverless data-integration service that delivers "30% lower pricing than previous AWS Glue versions and introduc[es] full support for Apache Iceberg v3 features," according to [AWS's official announcement](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/aws-glue-6-0-now-available-with-30-lower-price-and-full-apache-iceberg-v3-support/). The release, detailed in a blog post by AWS News Blog lead blogge...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-structured News article following the Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis template. Appropriate length (656 words, within the 400-1200 News range). Prose is factual and avoids sensationalism; the Analysis section offers reasonable, non-speculative industry context (open table format adoption, low-switching-cost upgrade pattern) without overstating certainty.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both sources were read directly from the committed gzip snapshots (not re-fetched live), and their sha256 hashes were independently recomputed and confirmed to match manifest.json exactly (source-0.html.gz: 7033dbc4...02e995; source-1.html.gz: 1953318233...de721d11). source-0.html.gz (aws.amazon.com AWS News Blog, 'AWS Glue 6.0 now available with 30% lower price and full Apache Iceberg v3 support', by Channy Yun, dated 21 AUG 2026) is the AWS primary announcement. source-1.html.gz (dbta.com, 'AWS Glue 6.0 is More Affordable and Now Offers Full Support for Apache Iceberg v3', by Stephanie Simone, dated Aug 24, 2026) is Database Trends and Applications' derivative/secondary coverage of the same announcement, explicitly attributing its facts to AWS ('According to AWS...', '...the company said') and linking back to aws.amazon.com for more information.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every direct quotation in the submission was checked verbatim against the AWS snapshot text and confirmed exact, including: '30% lower pricing than previous AWS Glue versions and introduc[es] full support for Apache Iceberg v3 features' (the bracketed [es] is a legitimate grammatical alteration of AWS's 'introducing', clearly marked); 'built on a fully modernized runtime, Apache Spark 4.1, Python 3.13, and Scala 2.13, delivering faster performance'; 'AWS Glue provides the most complete Iceberg v3 implementation on any fully serverless managed Spark service, along with new capabilities that simplify ETL authoring, improve PySpark performance, and enable real-time streaming with single-digit millisecond latency' (this passage is also quoted identically, word-for-word, in the DBTA snapshot -- confirming the article's claim that both outlets quote it identically); the VARIANT shredding quotes; the Geometry/Geography, nanosecond-precision timestamp, and unknown-type-handling bullet labels; the Spark Declarative Pipelines and Arrow-native UDF/UDTF quotes; and the real-time streaming mode quote. Iceberg 1.11.0 as the base version, the no-API-change upgrade path via --glue-version, and the Spark upgrade agent / auto-upgrade feature are all confirmed in the AWS snapshot. The 'AWS News Blog lead blogger' credit for Channy Yun matches the snapshot's author bio verbatim ('Channy is a Lead Blogger of AWS News Blog...'). Both 'What We Don't Know' claims were checked and hold: the AWS snapshot gives no benchmark figures for VARIANT query-performance gains or exact streaming latency beyond 'single-digit millisecond', and neither snapshot breaks down how the 30% price cut splits across Glue's billable components (the AWS snapshot only restates the general crawler/ETL-per-second and Data Catalog monthly-fee billing structure, not a component-level breakdown of the 30% reduction).
editor_notes.citation_attribution_check: Specifically verified per the review brief: the '30% lower pricing' and 'full Apache Iceberg v3 support' claims are quoted and attributed solely to 'AWS's official announcement' in the Overview paragraph -- '30%' appears exactly once in the article body, in that AWS-attributed quote, and is never separately sourced to or re-attributed to DBTA. DBTA is cited only for (a) independently corroborating that Glue 6.0 is generally available today in all regions, and (b) reporting the same Spark 4.1/Python 3.13/Scala 2.13 version numbers and the same identical 'most complete Iceberg v3 implementation' quote -- both are accurate characterizations of DBTA's snapshot content, which itself explicitly attributes its facts to AWS ('According to AWS...', 'the company said') rather than presenting them as DBTA's own reporting. DBTA is correctly used as corroboration of a derivative secondary source, not mistaken for the origin of AWS's own claims.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No editorializing, no unsourced superlatives beyond what AWS itself claims (properly hedged as AWS's own characterization, e.g. 'AWS is positioning managed Glue jobs as...'). No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for 'aws glue' and 'apache iceberg' (case-insensitive). No prior article covers AWS Glue 6.0 or this announcement -- this is a genuinely new topic. Related but distinct prior coverage exists: 2026-05/21-apache-iceberg-1110-ships-with-full-encryption-spark-41-support-and-deletion-vectors-for-flink.md (the Iceberg 1.11.0 release this Glue version is built on) and 2026-04/09-iceberg-summit-2026-draws-all-major-cloud-vendors-as-v3-adoption-accelerates-across-the-data-lakehouse-ecosystem.md (broader Iceberg v3 ecosystem trend). Neither overlaps with or duplicates this article's specific news event.

editor_notes.overall_assessment: High-quality, well-sourced submission. All direct quotes verified verbatim against the AWS primary source snapshot; the secondary DBTA source is genuinely corroborative and is not misused as the origin of AWS's own pricing or Iceberg-support claims. No unsourced specifics, no fabrications, no misattribution. Ready for publication as-is.
